author: Navjot Tomer (Mindstellar)
description_html:
PayPal Payment

Take payments for ShopClass shop orders and credit packages through PayPal Checkout. Buyers pay on PayPal's own pages, so no card or account details reach your site. When the buyer comes back, the plugin captures the payment and core adds the credits or marks the shop order paid. A verified webhook covers buyers who never come back.

Requirements

  • ShopClass 7.0.0 or later, with billing turned on
  • PHP 8.0 or later, with the curl extension
  • Cron running, for retries and the daily check of pending orders

It works on shared hosting: the daily check and webhook retries run on cron or core's auto-cron.

Install

From the admin: Plugins → Manage plugins → Browse, find PayPal Payment, then Install and activate it. Or upload the zip under Plugins → Add new.

Settings

  1. Open Settings → Billing → Payment methods and choose Set up next to PayPal Payment.
  2. At developer.paypal.com, open Apps & Credentials with Sandbox selected and create an app (or open the default one).
  3. Copy its Client ID and Secret into the Sandbox app fields.
  4. In the same app, add a webhook with the URL the settings page shows:
    https://example.com/index.php?page=billing&action=callback&gateway=paypal

    and subscribe it to these events:

  • CHECKOUT.ORDER.APPROVED
  • PAYMENT.CAPTURE.COMPLETED
  • PAYMENT.CAPTURE.DENIED
  • PAYMENT.CAPTURE.REFUNDED
  1. Copy the webhook's ID into Webhook ID and save. The Connection line on the settings page says whether the credentials and the webhook work. It is checked again after each save, and otherwise every ten minutes.

PayPal shows at checkout once the active mode has a client ID and a secret, and the site's billing currency is one PayPal takes. Live mode also needs a webhook ID. In sandbox it is optional, so a local site PayPal cannot reach still works: the buyer's return captures the payment.

The secret is never shown again. Leave its box blank to keep it.

Currencies

PayPal takes AUD, BRL, CAD, CHF, CNY, CZK, DKK, EUR, GBP, HKD, HUF, ILS, JPY, MXN, MYR, NOK, NZD, PHP, PLN, SEK, SGD, THB, TWD and USD. With any other billing currency the gateway is not offered. HUF, JPY and TWD are charged in whole units, so a package priced with a fraction in those currencies cannot be paid with PayPal.

Sandbox mode

The plugin starts in sandbox mode, and an admin notice says so. In sandbox mode only a signed-in admin sees PayPal at checkout, so a live site cannot give credits away. Pay with a sandbox buyer account.

To go live, switch PayPal's dashboard to Live, copy the live app's client ID and secret, add the same webhook to the live app, paste its ID, then switch Mode to Live.

How an order is paid

  • When the buyer comes back from PayPal, the plugin captures the payment and settles the order at once.
  • If the buyer closes the tab after approving, the CHECKOUT.ORDER.APPROVED webhook captures it. Captures that clear later, such as eChecks, arrive as PAYMENT.CAPTURE.COMPLETED.
  • A buyer who cancels at PayPal comes back to the buy page and the order is closed.
  • If the site cannot record a payment, the event is queued and retried, and PayPal sends it again. If it still fails, the site's contact address gets an e-mail.
  • Once a day, pending PayPal orders over an hour old are checked with PayPal. Orders the buyer never approved are closed after a day.
  • If a payment lands after its order was closed (the buyer cancelled in another tab, say), the plugin refunds it at PayPal at once and e-mails the site's contact address.

Every path goes through core's billing checks: amount, currency and owner must match, and a replayed event credits nothing. The plugin never captures money for an order that is no longer pending.

Refunds

Open the order under Billing → Orders and press Refund. The plugin refunds the whole payment at PayPal and core takes the credits back. If PayPal is still processing the refund, the order changes once PayPal reports it done. A full refund made in your PayPal account is recorded the same way. Partial refunds change nothing on the site.

Several sites, one PayPal account

Each site stores the PayPal order it created and ignores events for any other, and invoice ids carry a per-site prefix, so several sites can share an account. Give each site its own webhook.

What it stores

The credentials, mode and site id are preferences in the paypal section. An order keeps the PayPal order and mode in its meta. The access token is cached for its lifetime. Retries and the daily check are jobs in core's job queue. No table of its own.

Hooks

Registers the gateway on register_payment_gateways, adds the return and cancel pages, and listens to register_jobs, cron_daily and job_gave_up. It fires no hooks.

Uninstall

Uninstalling removes the plugin's settings, the saved secrets and the cached PayPal token. The site id is kept, so orders still in flight settle after a reinstall.

Translations

Copy languages/paypal.pot to languages/<locale>/messages.po, translate it, and compile it to messages.mo in the same folder. After changing strings, run php tools/make-pot.php.

Tests

./tests/run.sh                                  # unit tests, no network
php tests/integration/billing.php               # core's scratch MySQL on port 33061

Both load core from SHOPCLASS_CORE, or a sibling checkout named osclass.

License

GPL-3.0-or-later. See LICENSE.
name: PayPal Payment
short_description: Take payments for shop orders and credit packages through PayPal Checkout, with verified webhooks and refunds from the admin.

versions.changelog_html:
Changed

  • PayPal is offered for any order in a currency it takes, whatever the billing currency; credit packages need the billing currency to be one PayPal takes.
  • The settings page warns only when the billing currency is one PayPal cannot take.

Changed

  • On Shopclass 7.0 the settings page stays reachable from the plugin list, since 7.0 has no Billing menu for plugin pages.
  • On Shopclass 7.0 the daily check of pending orders is skipped instead of failing.
  • In sandbox mode PayPal is offered with only the client id and secret; live mode still needs the webhook id.
  • The settings page moves under Billing, and says why PayPal is not offered at checkout (unsupported currency, sandbox mode).
  • Sandbox mode also shows at checkout for a signed-in admin on themes that pay through the API (Shopclass 7.1).
